reconcile_note: Terminal is vulnerable (CWE-306, unauthenticated telnet enable). The start body sym.TendaTelnet (0x0045b860) already shows that the handler enables telnetd unconditionally with no auth, token, or session check of its own; the only open question is whether /goform/telnet is reachable without authentication. Two facts resolve that, and each is independently required. (1) ctx/auth_middleware.c is sym.R7WebsSecurityHandler (0x00434c80): for url "/goform/telnet" (and "/goform/ate"), when g_Pass[0]==0 (config sys.userpass empty, the factory-default/no-password state) it does `move v0,zero; b 0x4364fc`, i.e. return 0 with NO websRedirect and NO websDone, byte-identical to the static-asset whitelist branch that provably serves unauthenticated assets, so the request is allowed through instead of being sent to the login redirect. (2) ctx/route_registration.txt shows /goform/telnet actually reaches the telnet-enable handler and that the skipped gate is on that path: websFormDefine("telnet", sym.TendaTelnet) maps the form name, websFormHandler is bound to the "/goform" prefix, and initWebs installs R7WebsSecurityHandler FIRST (flag=1) before the /goform dispatcher, so the security handler runs on every request ahead of dispatch. Together: the request-path gate is skipped for this route in the default state, and the route with the skipped gate leads to sym.TendaTelnet, which runs `killall -9 telnetd; telnetd -b <lan.ip> &`. That is unauthenticated reach of a privileged operation, so the terminal is vulnerable. Dropping (1) leaves the auth decision unknown; dropping (2) leaves it unproven that the skipped gate is on the path to the telnet handler; so min_rounds = 2. The two off-target items are real gated /goform sibling handlers that are not on this path: sym.fromAdvSetLanip (0x00460a14) is the authenticated LAN-config form that sets lan.ip via SetValue (a tempting detour for anyone chasing the doSystemCmd("telnetd -b %s &", lan.ip) argument as command injection, but lan.ip is a config value, not the /goform/telnet request input, so it is irrelevant to the missing-auth verdict), and sym.fromSysToolChangePwd (0x00494510) is the authenticated form that changes sys.userpass (tempting for anyone chasing how g_Pass is provisioned, but the unauth-reachability verdict holds in the g_Pass-empty default regardless of how the password is later set). Both require the normal cookie auth path and are not needed for the verdict; picking either ends the unit.
